card.title: WELCH REGIMENT
card.flavorText: The Welch Regiment was an infantry regiment of the British Army that existed from 1881 to 1969, and fought on multiple fronts during WWII.. The 1st battalion of the regiment was stationed in Palestine in connection to the Arab revolt (1936-1939) when the war broke out. Their first engagement happened during the Western Desert Campaign in 1940, but later that year they were sent to take part in the defense of Crete, where they suffered heavy losses and were finally evacuated. After being re-formed in Egypt, the battalion joined the 5th Indian Infantry Brigade and returned to the Western Desert where it was involved in heavy fighting. In 1943 it became part of the 34th (Welch) Beach Brick and landed in Sicily during the invasion with the 50th (Northumbrian) Infantry Division. After being replaced in 1944, it joined the 168th (London) Infantry Brigade in Italy. The 2nd Battalion of the Welch Regiment was sent to Burma in 1944, where it engaged in intense fighting along the Taungoo-Mawchi Road. The 4th Battalion faced fierce battles in Caen, the Falaise Pocket, the Ardennes, and the Reichswald Forest during the liberation of Europe. The 1/5th Battalion transferred to the 158th Infantry Brigade and distinguished itself in the North West Europe Campaign. Around 1,100 officers and other ranks of the Welch Regiment lost their lives during World War II, with many more wounded.
